Google Meet attendance for CPE, CLE & CEU credit webinars

Organizations delivering live Continuing Professional Education (CPE for CPAs), Continuing Legal Education (CLE for attorneys), and Continuing Education Units (CEUs for engineers and realtors) over Google Meet must prove that attendees met minimum duration requirements before issuing certificates. Here is how to automate compliance logs.
Continuing Education Attendance Tracking
Audit-ready continuing education attendance export with exact minutes attended

Protect Your Provider Accreditation: Regulatory standards (such as NASBA for CPAs and State Bar associations) require documented verification of attendee connection duration (e.g. 50 minutes of active attendance per 1.0 CPE credit hour). Attendance Tracker delivers audit-ready spreadsheet records.
Continuing Education Compliance Requirements
50-Minute Hour Standard: NASBA rules calculate 1 CPE credit per 50 minutes of active learning. Providers need exact minutes logged for every participant.
Handling Drop-Offs & Disconnections: When an attendee's internet blips, their multiple session segments must be summed into a verified total.
Certificate Generation Roster: Program administrators need a clean spreadsheet with participant full names, emails, and verified completion flags.
How Attendance Tracker Automates CE Certification
1. Server-Side Duration Calculation
Using the official Google Meet REST API, Attendance Tracker calculates exact server-verified join times, leave times, and total minutes present for each registrant.
2. Formatted Google Sheets Export

When the webinar closes, a tabbed spreadsheet is instantly generated in your Google Drive. Each row contains the registrant's email, arrival timestamp, departure timestamp, and total minutes attended (e.g. 52 mins), making certificate issuance straightforward.
3. Multi-Session Conference Tracking
For multi-day professional conferences or 4-part webinar series, Attendance Tracker groups all sessions by Google Calendar recurring IDs to calculate overall conference credits per attendee.
